@graph.headline: Fence Rules by City in Oakland County: What Your City Actually Requires Before You Build
@graph.description: A city-by-city breakdown of residential fence rules across Oakland County, Michigan: the six-foot ceiling, front-yard limits, corner-lot sight triangles, permit fees, easement approvals, and HOA overlays, with ordinance sections cited for Auburn Hills, Rochester Hills, Rochester, Troy, Novi, and Bloomfield Township.

about.name: Residential fence zoning and permitting across Oakland County, Michigan, including Auburn Hills Zoning Ordinance sections 1902 and 1904 (6-foot side and rear height, 2.5-foot opaque and 4-foot non-opaque front yard limits, berm-inclusive height measurement, 25-foot corner visibility triangle with a 30-inch cap), Rochester Hills Zoning Ordinance 138-10.107 and 138-5.204 (6-foot side and rear, 3-foot front and side-street setback, obscuring fence restriction between the house and setback line, prohibitions on wire, barbed wire, spikes and electric fences, non-residential 8-foot and 10-foot security fence limits), City of Rochester zoning permit requirements, Troy City Code Chapter 83 (6-foot maximum, 30 inches in front of the front building setback line, 48-inch non-obscuring corner fence allowance, final lot grade and easement permits, 7-foot Michigan Building Code threshold), Novi Zoning Code 5.11 (6-foot maximum, front yard setback limits, corner lot prohibition, 2-acre and 200-foot frontage exceptions, material and uniformity rules), Bloomfield Township Zoning Ordinance Chapter 42 Section 5.7 with 16-foot side and 25-foot rear dog containment setbacks and Zoning Board of Appeals review, 2015 Michigan Residential Code R105.2 and R403.1.4, MISS DIG 811 dig notice requirements under MCL 460.725 and PA 174 of 2013, 2015 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code Section 305 pool barriers, and Michigan HOA deed restriction overlays

mainEntity.name: How tall can my fence be in Oakland County, Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Six feet along side and rear lot lines is the standard across Auburn Hills, Rochester Hills, Rochester, Troy, Novi, and Bloomfield Township. Fences seven feet and taller leave the state's building-permit exemption under the 2015 Michigan Residential Code R105.2 and require a building permit with plan review.

mainEntity.name: Can I put a fence in my front yard?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, and the limits are tight. Auburn Hills allows opaque fences to 2.5 feet and non-opaque to four feet in the required front yard. Rochester Hills allows three feet in the front or side-street setback and no obscuring fence over three feet between the house and the setback line. Troy caps front-of-setback fences at 30 inches. Novi generally prohibits front-yard fencing except on lots over two acres or with 200 or more feet of plat frontage.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit for a six-foot wood fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in every city covered here. The state building-code exemption for fences under seven feet does not replace the local zoning or land-use permit, and each city requires its own application, plot plan, and inspection, several with a final inspection after installation.

mainEntity.name: How much does a fence permit cost in Oakland County?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the city. Troy publishes $150 for fences under 300 linear feet and $200 over 300 feet. Bloomfield Township charges $30 plan review plus $120 for a fence or dog-containment permit. Other cities publish fees on their own schedules, so call the building department before budgeting and never treat an aggregator website's number as current.

mainEntity.name: What are the fence rules for a corner lot?

acceptedAnswer.text: Auburn Hills and Rochester Hills both prohibit anything above 30 inches from street grade inside a 25-foot sight triangle measured along each right-of-way line at an intersection. Novi prohibits corner-lot fencing beyond the front and exterior side setbacks. Troy allows a non-obscuring fence up to 48 inches along the common street line on qualifying double-setback corner lots. Corner lots are the most common source of fence complaints in the county.

mainEntity.name: Does my HOA have to approve my fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your subdivision has deed restrictions or bylaws covering fencing, yes, and the city permit does not substitute for it. Novi requires HOA approval where applicable, Bloomfield Township requires subdivision association comments in the permit file, and Troy recommends the check in writing. Where the association is stricter than the city, the association's rule controls in practice.

mainEntity.name: How far from the property line does a dog fence have to be in Bloomfield Township?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sixteen feet from side lot lines and 25 feet from the rear lot line, for both standard and invisible dog-containment fences. An invisible fence may run around the front of the house to complete the circuit if it stays within five feet of the house. Standard visible dog fences require Zoning Board of Appeals approval as well as an ordinance permit.

mainEntity.name: Can I build a fence inside an easement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not without approval. Troy will not issue a fence permit for construction inside an easement without the Director of Public Works' approval, and the same practical restriction applies almost everywhere, because a utility with an easement can remove a fence built over it. Check your plot plan for drainage and utility easements before finalizing the fence line.
